leaps.title: Leap #1 - The World of Sensations
leaps.description: As a consequence of eye development, your baby becomes more interested in their environment. Their vision range increases beyond 20-30 centimeters. Due to lacrimal gland development, their eyes begin producing tears. The tears help lubricate their eyes, remove irritants, and aid their immune system.
whatToExpect: Baby may be more fussy and clingy

leaps.title: Leap #2 - The World of Patterns
leaps.description: During this transition, your baby starts developing movement consciously rather than reflectively. They might momentarily lift their head during tummy time and turn towards sounds. They might move and look curiously at both sides of their hands. They now start feeling the movement of their body parts.
newSkills: Can lift head briefly during tummy time

leaps.title: Leap #3 - The World of Smooth Transitions
leaps.description: Your infant's brain has grown by 25% compared to their due date brain size. Senses like vision and hearing clarity are sharpening. Motion developments let your baby move smoother and less robotic. They might start grabbing, holding, and tasting things by putting them into their mouth.
newSkills: Puts things in mouth to explore

leaps.title: Leap #4 - The World of Events
leaps.description: Your baby starts searching for their caretaker and following them with their eyes. Their upgraded motion control enables them to move all body limbs and pass things from one hand to the other. They see, scent, feel, and taste better. They might start waving and changing facial expressions.

leaps.title: Leap #5 - The World of Relationships
leaps.description: Your baby starts understanding relationships between things. Most importantly, this is when your baby understands the idea of distance. They might protest when you leave the room. Motion control is now even better.
whatToExpect: Cries when you leave the room
newSkills: Knows objects still exist when hidden

leaps.title: Leap #6 - The World of Categories
leaps.description: This period is considered the continuation of Leap 5. Your baby begins paying closer attention to the distance between themselves and their caretakers. They might resist putting themselves to sleep unless caretakers are close enough.

leaps.title: Leap #7 - The World of Sequences
leaps.description: Your infant is growing strong and more confident in their movements. They might try to stand aided by you and try to crawl. Balance is developing. They start inspecting things closely - you might see them examining small details like hair on the floor.

leaps.title: Leap #8 - The World of Programs
leaps.description: The last transition before your infant becomes a toddler. Your baby is now strong enough to explore the world and have opinions. They understand sequential event flows and might refuse their everyday routine. They enjoy meeting new things and going places.
